newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee gains on dollar's lethargy.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee gains on dollar's lethargy.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee rose on Tuesday as banks sold dollars due to the greenback's overseas lethargy, dealers said.
At 0445 GMT the rupee was at 58.50 to the dollar, after opening at its previous closing level of 58.60, they said.
"Banks are selling dollars on its overseas weakness and the Central Bank's action," said a Union Bank dealer.
The Central Bank's dollar-rupee exchange rate was unchanged, leaving buying and selling prices at 58.1848 and 59.3602.
Overnight call money rates were volatile as lenders dominated the market and banks covered positions ahead of two mid-week holidays, dealers said.
"Today being squaring up day because Wednesday and Thursday are holidays, has also put pressure on call rates which were stretched due to the holidays," said a Citibank dealer.
It is customary for banks to face extra cash withdrawals in the run-up to holidays, he noted.
